question: Is there an age limit to live in the ACity hostel?
answer: Yes. Students must not be above the age of 24 at the time of checking in to the hostel, and must remain under 25 for at least 6 months after checking in. This is a formal condition stated in the Housing Application Form. Students who do not meet this age requirement are not eligible for on-campus hostel accommodation. Contact sca@acity.edu.gh for alternative arrangements.

question: What are the steps for an international student to regularise their stay in Ghana after arriving at ACity?
answer:
International students must complete two steps:

Step 1 — Non-Citizenship Card (within 20 days of arrival):
• Visit the National Identification Authority (NIA) at Ghana Immigration Service with your international passport
• Pay USD 120 — NIA captures your bio data and issues the card
• File a hard copy of the card and passport with ACity's Registry
• Registry issues your introductory letter for your Residence Permit
• Renew annually for USD 60

Step 2 — Residence Permit (within 25 days of arrival):
• Visit the Ghana Immigration Service (GIS) in North Ridge with all required documents
• Complete the immigration form and pay the prescribed fee
• GIS issues the Residence Permit after approximately four weeks
• Alternatively: submit documents to the SCA office by the communicated deadline

For questions: sca@acity.edu.gh
For GTEC matters: Ms. Irene Aforve — irene.aforve@acity.edu.gh | +233 245 944 559
keywords: international student procedure, regularise stay, NIA card, residence permit, Ghana immigration

question: How much does a Residence Permit cost for international students in Ghana?
answer:
Residence Permit fees (payable to Ghana Immigration Service):

• ECOWAS Nationals without Ghana Card: GHS 500
• ECOWAS Nationals with Ghana Card: GHS 400
• Non-ECOWAS/Foreign Nationals without Ghana Card: GHS 560
• Non-ECOWAS/Foreign Nationals with Ghana Card: GHS 460
• Administrative Fee (all applicants): GHS 200

Penalty for overstaying without a valid permit:
• ECOWAS: GHS 200/month
• Non-ECOWAS: GHS 300/month

Contact: sca@acity.edu.gh

question: What is the AC sensor policy in ACity hostel rooms?
answer:
ACity is implementing Sensibo Sky AC Sensors in hostel rooms as part of a sustainability initiative to reduce energy consumption. The sensor enforces a temperature range of 21°C (minimum) to 25°C (maximum).

Key rules:
1. Students must NOT tamper with, remove, disable, cover, or interfere with the sensor in any way
2. Tampering includes: physically removing, covering, disconnecting from power or Wi-Fi, or attempting to reconfigure the device
3. Any tampering is treated as intentional damage to university property — the student is liable for the full replacement cost PLUS charged double that amount as a deterrent
4. Regular monitoring is conducted and violations result in disciplinary action per the code of conduct

Students must sign the AC Sensor Agreement upon checking in.
keywords: AC sensor, Sensibo, hostel AC, temperature control, AC tampering, AC policy
